Man Pulls Off Heist, Buys Almost-New Chevrolet Corvette Z06 for $25,000 Below MSRP
23 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Every which way you spin it, this transaction looks like a steal. Even when you factor in the buyer's fee. Technically, the auction did close at roughly $25,000 under MSRP, but in reality, the buyer still had to pay a fee to the auction site. Regardless, it's an almost-new Z06 at a significant discount, and I don't know anyone who'd pass up such a deal.
I don't even mind the spec. Sure, it doesn't have additional carbon fiber elements or the Z07 package, and it's not a 3LZ variant, but you still get the bare minimum, and then some (like the optional front-axle lift system and GT2 bucket seats). These types of deals are very sought-after in the industry. It's not about lowballing the seller, as much as simply getting the most bang for your buck, which I believe is what happened here.
Could this Z06 have sold for even less? I guess it's possible, but not by much. Maybe another couple of grand at the absolute most. Keep in mind that it's barely been driven.
The Torch Red exterior is one controversial aspect to contend with, but that's such an easy fix - you just get it wrapped in whatever color you want and problem fixed! If you can afford a car for $110k+ (which is what this cost, buyer's fee included), you can certainly afford a $5k+ wrap from a quality shop. Then again, maybe you like the bright red exterior and you just leave it as-is.
Aside from its vibrant colorway, this Z06 Coupe also comes with Carbon Flash accents, a rear spoiler, LED headlights, front and rear cameras, plus a set of optional black-finished 20" front and 21" rear forged wheels wearing Michelin rubber and Brembo discs with red-finished calipers. I already mentioned the front-axle lift system, which comes with memory settings. It's a must-have as far as I'm concerned.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Meanwhile, interior highlights include the Jet Black leather GT2 bucket seats (heated/ventilated), the Stealth Interior Trim Package, keyless entry, a performance data and video recorder, dual-zone automatic climate control, cruise control, a Bose sound system, a head-up display, heated and leather-wrapped steering wheel, and a wide range of electronic driver aids such as lane-keep assist, rear cross-traffic alert, side blind-zone alert, and forward collision alert.
If you look at the mid-mounted 5.5-liter LT6 V8 engine, you'll notice the optional red intake and compartment accent lighting. On paper, this car is putting down 670 horsepower and 460 lb-ft of torque, with everything getting sent to the rear wheels via an eight-speed dual-clutch automatic transmission.
In a straight line, the C8 Z06 can rocket to 60 mph (97 kph) in just 2.6 seconds (with a 1-foot rollout), before maxing out at 195 mph (314 kph).
